title: Right cones take monomorphisms to right anodyne maps
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices and horns as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For simplicial sets $X,Y$, define their join by $(X\star Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{u+v+1=r}X_u\times Y_v$, with simplicial operators induced by restricting the ordered concatenation of the $X$-vertices followed by the $Y$-vertices. Write $X^{\triangleright}=X\star\Delta^0$, with $X$ as its base and the additional vertex as its cone point. Call a simplicial map right anodyne if it belongs to the smallest class containing all isomorphisms and all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. For every simplicial map $u:A\to B$ that is injective in every simplicial degree, the induced map $u^{\triangleright}=u\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}:A^{\triangleright}\to B^{\triangleright}$ is right anodyne.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 4.3.7.8 (0196), first assertion. The convention for right anodyne is Variant 4.2.4.2. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Online text read; archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $u:A\hookrightarrow B$. This gives $Z_0\cong A$, a sequence with colimit $B$, and each $Z_n\hookrightarrow Z_{n+1}$ a pushout of a coproduct of $n$-boundary inclusions. Refine each such successor into individual attachments: well-order its set of cells and, starting with $Z_n$, attach the cells successively along their given boundary maps into $Z_n$. At a limit take the union. A map out of the resulting object is exactly a map out of $Z_n$ and one map from each attached simplex agreeing on its boundary, so the resulting object is the prescribed pushout $Z_{n+1}$. Concatenating these well-ordered refinements gives a continuous transfinite sequence from $A$ to $B$ whose successor maps are pushouts of single boundary inclusions. If there are no cells, the corresponding map is an isomorphism. The endpoint identification with $B$ identifies the structural map from $A$ with $u$, since each intermediate pushout comparison agrees with the given maps into $B$.

source.place: Proposition 1.5.5.14, relative skeletal filtration and well-ordering of its cells

proof.text: Put $C(X)=X\star\Delta^0$. In degree $r$ the explicit join formula identifies $C(X)_r$ with one cone-point simplex and a disjoint copy of $X_k$ for each $0\leq k\leq r$; the $k=r$ copy is the pure base. For every map $X\to Y$, the cone-point simplex is fixed and each $X_k$ maps to $Y_k$ with its label $k$ unchanged. Thus for a pushout span $Y\leftarrow X\to Z$, the degreewise pushout of cones has one common cone-point simplex and, separately at each label $k$, the set pushout $Y_k\amalg_{X_k}Z_k$. This is exactly $C(Y\amalg_X Z)_r$. For a monotone map $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$, a simplex $x\in X_k$ of label $k$ goes to the cone-point simplex if $\alpha^{-1}([k])$ is empty; otherwise write this initial segment as $[\ell]$, and its image is $X(\alpha|_{[\ell]})(x)$ of label $\ell$. The cone-point simplex always maps to the cone-point simplex. This formula commutes with the pushout comparisons, since every map of simplicial sets commutes with restriction. In any nonempty ordinal chain the cone-point simplices are all identified with one point and each fixed-label summand has the colimit of the corresponding $X_k$. Hence coning preserves pushouts and the nonempty limit-ordinal colimits needed in Step 1. Coning also preserves isomorphisms by applying it to the inverse. The same restriction formula commutes with these colimit comparisons, so these too are simplicial identifications.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.7.8: expansion of weak saturation using the explicit join formula

proof.text: Use the simplex and horn definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A monotone map $[r]\to[n+1]$ has a unique initial segment landing in $[n]$ and complementary final segment landing in the last vertex. This identifies $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0$ with $\Delta^{n+1}$, respecting operators by restriction of segments. Its subcomplex $\partial\Delta^n\star\Delta^0$ consists exactly of maps omitting at least one vertex of $[n]$: this is true for the pure base summand by the boundary definition, for mixed simplices by their boundary base factor, and for the pure cone summand since it omits every base vertex. Thus the subcomplex is the union of the faces opposite vertices $0,\ldots,n$, namely $\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}$. For $n=0$ it is the final vertex of $\Delta^1$. Its index satisfies $0<n+1\leq n+1$, so every coned boundary inclusion is a generating right horn.

Cone the continuous single-cell sequence of Step 1. Step 2 identifies its initial object with $A^{\triangleright}$, its final object with $B^{\triangleright}$, every successor with a pushout of the coned boundary inclusion, and every nonzero limit with the required colimit. Step 3 makes each nonidentity successor a pushout of a generating right horn. The definition of right anodyne in the statement therefore includes every successor and their transfinite composite. That composite is precisely $u\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}$ by the naturality of the degreewise identifications, proving the assertion.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 4.3.7.8 first assertion, expanded from the relative skeletal filtration and generating right-horn calculation
